newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FEATURE - For Europe, APEC one more eastern mystery.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - For Europe, APEC one more eastern mystery.

text.p: Ask all but the most well-informed European for a description of APEC and the best you might hope for is "the Asia something-or-other".
More likely, there will be a mystified silence, such is the lack of awareness in Europe of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, analysts say.
"In Europe there is a great deal of ignorance about APEC," said Jacques Pelkmans, analyst at the Brussels-based think tank European Institute for Asia Studies.
"Most Europeans think it is an Asian group... very few realise it includes the whole of North America and a few others besides," he added.
A special seminar on "APEC and Europe" in Brussels last month drew just a handful of experts -- all of whom agreed that the European Union was ignoring the group at its peril.

Analysts say the EU -- which has battled for decades to build its own free-trade community -- has a tendency to dismiss the importance of APEC because its consensus approach results in non-binding agreements that legalistic Europeans regard as worthless.
But experts in the European Commission -- the EU's executive -- relish the thought of some day being able to negotiate trade deals with a larger bloc rather than on a country-by-country basis.

APEC's strengths, say European analysts, are that it is drawn from a high-growth area, is business-driven, displays consensus flexibility, is a natural trading bloc, is made up of some of the leading economic powers and is backed by political leaders.
Its weaknesses, they say, are a lack of commitment, its sheer size and diversity, a lack of institutional machinery, built-in regionalism and its dominance by China, Japan and the U.S.

"Many of these arguments have been used in the past when describing the European Community," said Pelkmans. "But the EU now has history on its side. It is already a pretty efficient bloc with real, concrete benefits."

APEC, on the other hand, is considered by many outsiders to be a giant talking shop, he said, where rhetoric dominates and Asian leaders, indulged by Washington, get to beat the drum and complain about European interference.
Conscious of this, European officials have made a great effort to get closer to the powers that make up APEC.

The EU's transatlantic alliance with the United States is probably the world's most muscular trade partnership, while European leaders have since last year taken steps to boost their Asian ties through ASEM, the fledgling Asia-Europe Meeting.
The inaugural ASEM conference in Bangkok this year underscored growing European awareness that ignoring Asia could have adverse effects in both business and political arenas.
What exactly does APEC mean to Europe?

Pelkmans argues that echoes of "fortress Europe" in which the EU is now probably the world's most pro-active champion of trade liberalisation -- especially on so-called "new issues" such as the environment and labour rights -- mean APEC will always regard the 15-nation bloc with suspicion.
APEC is also wary of the EU getting a free ride on its own trade liberalisation moves, but is prepared to signal to the rest of the world that the area will remain devoted to unfettered growth.

Europe, Pelkmans argues, should realise also that Asian nations within APEC see the forum as an opportunity to flex their geo-political muscle and should avoid dismissing the contribution it can make to regional security.
"One way or another, the EU will be confronted with APEC for a long time to come," said Pelkmans. "The time for neglect is over."
